body.title: perf(api): reuse connections across API clients
body.description:
## Description

* perf(api): keep up to 25 idle connections per host

Clients from one factory now share a transport, so concurrent fan-out
(MRsFromArgs, IssuesFromArgs) draws on a single pool. Go's default of
two idle connections per host closed the rest after each round and made
the next round dial again over HTTP/1.1.

* perf(api): reuse connections across API clients

Every api.NewClient call built its own http.Transport, so each
Factory.GitLabClient() / Factory.ApiClient() call paid for a new TCP and
TLS handshake. `glab mr view 1` used three connections for its three
requests (MR lookup, approvals, telemetry).

The factory now owns an api.TransportCache, and clients it builds share
one transport whenever their transport settings (proxy, CA, client
certificate, skip_tls_verify, gitlab.com cipher suites) match. A
per-client wrapper hides CloseIdleConnections, which go-retryablehttp
calls after failed requests, so one client cannot drain the shared pool.
Clients built outside the factory keep a private transport.

At 50ms RTT against a mock GitLab: mr view 399ms -> 275ms,
mr list 276ms -> 214ms.

body.title: ci(snap): allow edge snap release to fail pending store review
body.description:
## What

Sets `allow_failure: true` on `snapcraft_release_edge`.

## Why

https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4031 added a `kube-config` `personal-files` plug (for https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8304). The Snap Store requires a snap declaration for that interface, so every upload fails automated review and is held for manual review. Starting with revision 6944, this makes `snapcraft_release_edge` fail on every `main` pipeline.

We're requesting the declaration on forum.snapcraft.io. Revert this change once the store grants it.

body.title: chore(deps): update module gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/v3 to v3.25.0
body.description:
Supersedes https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4126, whose `golangci-lint` job fails ([job](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-renovate-forks/cli/-/jobs/17215721873)):

```
internal/api/pipeline.go:73:10: SA1019: ListPipelineBridges is deprecated: the bridges route is deprecated in GitLab 19.2, use ListPipelineTriggerJobs instead. To be removed in client-go v4.0. (staticcheck)
```

## Changes

- Bump `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/v3` from v3.23.0 to v3.25.0.
- Add a `//nolint:staticcheck` with a reason on the `ListPipelineBridges` call.

## Why not migrate to `ListPipelineTriggerJobs`

It calls `/pipelines/:id/trigger_jobs`, which exists only in GitLab 19.2 and later. Switching now would break `glab ci view` for bridge jobs on older self-managed instances. The deprecated route keeps working until client-go v4, and we can migrate then (or add a version-gated fallback).

body.title: feat: support setting work item iteration id
body.description:
## Description

Add an `--iteration <id>` flag to `glab work-items create` and `glab work-items update`, so you can schedule a work item in an iteration without using the UI or GraphQL.

- The flag takes the numeric iteration ID, which `glab iteration list -F json` shows. It doesn't look up iterations by title, because iterations from automatic cadences have no title.
- The value goes to `IterationID` on `gitlab.CreateWorkItemOptions` and `gitlab.UpdateWorkItemOptions`. Both already exist in the pinned `client-go` v3.23.0, so no dependency bump is needed.
- Both commands use `Flags().Changed("iteration")` to tell whether the flag was set, so leaving it out never sends an iteration.
- `docs/source/work-items/` is regenerated with `make gen-docs`.

Removing an iteration is out of scope. `client-go` omits a nil `IterationID`, so it can't send the `null` that GraphQL needs to clear the field.

## Related Issues

Resolves #8622

## How has this been tested?

- New unit tests in `create_test.go` and `update_test.go`, using the `client-go` mocks through `cmdtest.SetupCmdForTest`:
  - `TestWorkItems{Create,Update}_Iteration`: `--iteration 123` sends `IterationID` `123`, and leaving the flag out sends no `IterationID`.
  - `TestWorkItems{Create,Update}_FlagValidation`: a non-numeric `--iteration` value is rejected.
- `go test ./internal/commands/workitems/...` passes.
- `golangci-lint run --new-from-rev=origin/main ./internal/commands/workitems/...` (2.14.0, Go 1.27.2) reports 0 issues.
- `make check-args check-embed` passes.

body.title: fix(mcp): link the deprecation feedback issue in the warning
body.description:
## Description

Adds a link to the `glab mcp` deprecation feedback issue (#8618) to the deprecation warning, so users who still rely on `glab mcp serve` can tell us what they'd miss. A separate feedback issue keeps this apart from general GitLab MCP Server feedback, as suggested in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8583#note_4013602044.

Running `glab mcp serve` now prints:

```plaintext
Command "serve" is deprecated, use the GitLab MCP Server (https://docs.gitlab.com/user/model_context_protocol/mcp_server/) instead. Share feedback in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8618.
```

`glab mcp` prints the same message with `"mcp"`.

## Related Issues

Related to #8583

## How has this been tested?

- Built `glab` and ran `glab mcp serve` and `glab mcp`: both print the message above on stderr.
- `make gen-docs` produces no changes, because deprecated commands have no generated pages.
- Pre-commit and pre-push hooks pass.
